messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT P1 — Canary error rate spike detected for checkout-service rollout (canary variant v2b). 5min error rate 11.8% (> alert threshold 5%). Auto-fallback triggered to fallback policy 'sticky-old-variant'.

bob.r: pinging on-call ml (@carla.p) and on-call infra (@fiona.sre). I'm seeing increased 502s and mismatched model-variant signatures in logs.

alice.m: acknowledged — i'm on it, switching to incident channel. Can someone paste the rollout policy?

carla.p: grabbing logs now. short summary from initial glance: canary v2b is returning a new response header X-Model-Variant: v2b, but the fallback/sticky mapping is pinning traffic to v1a for a subset of users, causing model mismatch in the smart-routing layer. That mismatch is manifesting as 502/500 from the translator proxy because schemas differ.

dan.oncall: seeing region fallback churn - requests from eu-west kept failing on v2b and were being routed to us-east fallback, then sticky affinites pinned them back to the failing host -> increased latency, repeated evictions. Looks like sticky TTL is long.

eve.prodeng: customers reporting checkout timeouts. I'm triaging customer impact now. Preliminary: 3 enterprise tenants experienced sustained failures between T+00:04 and T+00:12 (timeouts, repeated retries).

alice.m: putting this as P1. Steps: 1) pause rollout canary, 2) disable sticky fallback affinity, or reduce TTL to 0 to force fresh routing, 3) if needed, rollback canary variant to v2a. Any objections?

fiona.sre: +1 to pause rollout. I can run sticky-evict for the checkout prefix. Command i'll run: 
```
# admin evict sticky affinities for prefix
curl -X POST https://admin.internal.routing/evict_sticky -H 'Authorization: Bearer $SVC_TOKEN' -d '{"prefix":"checkout-service","scope":"all"}'
```
I'll also set a temporary routing override to prefer stable variant in eu-west: 
```
POST /routing/override
{ "prefix": "checkout-service", "policy": "prefer-stable", "expires_in": 600 }
```

bob.r: i'm checking the canary model logs — v2b shows a late regression in tokenizer preproc that triggers schema mismatch for certain inputs. That explains why certain sessions break.

deploy-bot: canary deployment paused by alice.m (reason: P1 rollback hold).

carla.p: after eviction we still saw some sticky reaffinities coming back because the rollout policy had fallback=sticky-old and sticky_ttl=86400 in the config. here's the relevant snippet from the policy: 
```
routing:
  policy: rollout
  canary_variant: v2b
  stable_variant: v1a
  fallback: sticky-old
  sticky_ttl: 86400
```
We need to change fallback to immediate-failover or set sticky_ttl=0.

alice.m: i've updated the routing override to set sticky_ttl=0 for checkout-service and switched fallback to immediate-failover. Changes pushed.

fiona.sre: evict completed (job id: evict-248900-01). Observed drop in 502s within 30s. p95 latency dropped from 1200ms -> 350ms over next 2 mins.

bob.r: confirmed schema regression in v2b tokenizer. We'll rollback the canary to v2a and mark v2b blocked from rollouts until patch.

dan.oncall: region churn stopped after override. No more fallback loops. eu-west -> stable routing assert shows 98% of requests hitting v1a.

eve.prodeng: notifying impacted customers: three tenants experienced ~8-10 min degraded window. we've opened support cases CS-6371, CS-6372, CS-6373. Customer-facing note drafted, will send after post-incident summary.

alice.m: rolling back canary to v2a now. Command: `redwoodctl rollout abort --prefix checkout-service --to-variant v1a --reason "P1: schema regression v2b"`

deploy-bot: rollback initiated (rollout-id: r-248900-9).

fiona.sre: monitoring metrics. Error rate back to baseline (0.3%) and stability restored.

bob.r: filing a follow-up bug for tokenizer change and adding pre-deploy schema/e2e tests to catch variant signature mismatches.

carla.p: suggested RCA notes: 
- Root cause: tokenizer schema change in v2b introduced incompatible response shape for a subset of inputs. 
- Contributing factor: rollout policy used sticky fallback with very long TTL (86400s) which pinned some sessions to older variant and created oscillating fallback across regions. 
- Mitigation that worked: pause canary, evict sticky affinities, set sticky_ttl=0, switch fallback to immediate-failover, rollback canary.
- Action items: add variant signature invariant check in pre-rollout CI; add autopause on schema-change-detect; lower default sticky_ttl for rollout fallbacks to 300s; add an SLO-based canary block rule.

alice.m: declaring incident resolved. Resolution time: 2489014820.

eve.prodeng: severity = P1. Impact summary to include in incident page: 3 enterprise tenants impacted, visible for ~8-12 minutes, increased 502s and p95 latency spikes to 1200ms. No data loss reported.

fiona.sre: creating follow-up ticket INT-248900 with action items and owners.

bob.r: thanks team. postmortem RFC will be filed in 48h, will include suggested automation. :white_check_mark:
